title: Reading Too Much Into It? Interpretive Preferences and Commitment in LLM Mentalisation under Ambiguity
abstract: arXiv:2610.28105v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for interpersonal advice, potentially shaping how users interpret ambiguous social encounters. Existing Theory of Mind evaluations typically rely on predefined answers, while uncertainty research overlooks LLMs' preferred explanations and confidence under psychological distress. To address these gaps, we introduce MentalLoom, a novel evaluation of LLM mentalisation comprising 604 ambiguous social episodes, matched depression and social anxiety disclosures, and four-turn dialogues with unchanged event evidence. translated_title: 过度解读了吗？模糊情境下大语言模型心理化中的解释偏好与承诺
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于提供人际建议，可能影响用户如何解读模糊的社会情境。现有的心智理论评估通常依赖于预设答案，而不确定性研究则忽视了LLM在心理困扰情境下偏好的解释及其置信度。为弥补这些空白，我们提出了MentalLoom，一种新颖的LLM心智化评估方法，包含604个模糊社会事件、匹配的抑郁症与社交焦虑自我披露，以及事件证据保持不变的四轮对话。在八个LLM上的实验显示，自我披露信息总体上最初引发了更多负面解释，但对叙述者本人的解读则更为积极。脚本化的重复提问表明，在没有新事件证据的情况下，模型表现出更多的情感支持、更强的对叙述者的积极认同以及更高的确定性。这些发现表明，用户语境能够重塑模型的解释偏好与承诺。
tldr: 该研究提出MentalLoom评估框架，发现在模糊社会情境下，用户的心理困扰披露与重复提问会促使八个主流LLM转向更积极的对叙述者的解读、提供更多情感支持并表现出更高的确定性，证明用户语境能够重塑模型的解释偏好与承诺。
en_tdlr: Introducing MentalLoom, a novel evaluation showing that across eight LLMs, user disclosures of psychological distress and repeated questioning without new evidence reshape interpretive preferences, eliciting more positive narrator-directed interpretations, greater emotional support, and higher certainty under ambiguity.
